testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Stay a safe distance behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay a safe distance behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, keep plenty of space between your vehicle and theirs.

questions.question: Why should you do a pre-trip inspection in the same order every time?

options.text: You are less likely to forget a step.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are less likely to forget a step.
questions.explanation: Using the same order each time helps you remember all the steps and makes it harder to miss anything.

questions.question: How do you complete an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull forward straight, then back up to the left.
Back up straight, then pull forward to the left.
Pull forward straight, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward straight, then back up to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left maneuver, first pull straight forward, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must fit completely within the parking space.

questions.question: How should pre-trip inspections be done?

options.text: Never the same way twice in a row.
In the same order every time.
Only if you think something is wrong with the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Do your inspection in the same order each time. This helps you learn the steps and remember to check everything.

questions.question: If other vehicles have trouble passing your truck on a multi-lane road, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane if your truck is moving slowly. Let other vehicles pass using the left lane.

questions.question: What is true about off-ramps for trucks?

options.text: They are usually safe for trucks.
They can be dangerous for trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be dangerous for trucks.
questions.explanation: On-ramps and off-ramps can be risky for trucks. Speed limits for ramps may be safe for cars but too fast for trucks.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Stop driving and get sleep if you feel tired. Continuing to drive while tired is dangerous. Coffee cannot replace sleep.

questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
When there is extra space on a truck.
Only when hazardous materials weigh more than 200 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Use warning placards any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials. Placards must be shown on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: What does fresh oil under your vehicle mean during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: A problem.
questions.explanation: Check under your vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks. Finding any of these is a problem you must address before driving.

questions.question: What should you check on power steering hoses?

options.text: For the right amount of brake fluid.
That they connect to the battery.

questions.correctAnswerText: For leaks.
questions.explanation: Check power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look especially for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: When using ABS brakes, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way you would in any vehicle. Do not change your braking technique when using ABS.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift.
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Help remove water and oil from air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help remove water and oil from air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil that can damage the brake system if they build up. Air tanks have drain valves to remove this water and oil.

questions.question: When you skid from going too fast, you can usually fix it by:

options.text: Removing your foot from the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Removing your foot from the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Remove your foot from the accelerator to stop the skid. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) does not need to include which item?

options.text: Number of meals eaten by the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Number of meals eaten by the driver
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include the trip origin, destination, Vehicle Identification Number, distance traveled, and fuel purchased. It does not need to include meals.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are okay to use on rear tires.
Are okay to use when carrying heavy loads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not safe to use.
questions.explanation: Never use wheels or rims that have been welded. They are not safe.

questions.question: Parked delivery trucks can be hazardous because:

options.text: People leaving the truck may be in a hurry and not check for other vehicles.
Packages often fall out onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: People leaving the truck may be in a hurry and not check for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The driver or worker may be in a hurry and pull into traffic without warning or step out without checking for passing vehicles.

questions.question: Front wheel brakes work:
questions.correctAnswerText: In all conditions.
questions.explanation: Front wheel brakes work well on all road conditions, even ice. Front wheel skids are unlikely.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, you should:

options.text: Keep driving and fix the brakes within a week.
Pull over and check the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: Stop the vehicle safely as soon as possible while you still have brake control. Check and repair the brakes right away.

questions.question: People working on a broken-down vehicle:

options.text: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
Do not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people fixing a broken-down vehicle on the roadside. They may be focused on the repair and not paying attention to passing traffic.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive on a tire missing one or two lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring on a rim is safe if you drive slower than 55 mph.
A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Cracked or bent lock rings are also dangerous. Check your tires and rims before driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: Which is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tires from different manufacturers
questions.explanation: Inspect your tires carefully before each trip. Tire sizes must match. Tires must not be cut, cracked, or damaged.

questions.question: Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.correctAnswerText: One half
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums during your walk-around inspection before driving. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle and you do not know how to put it out, you should:

options.text: Move away from the fire and wait for firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away from the fire and wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure how to put out a fire, do not try. Move away and let firefighters handle it. This is especially important for hazardous materials fires.

questions.question: A safety belt:

options.text: Keeps a driver secure during a crash.
Allows a driver to move around the vehicle during a crash.
Makes it hard for a driver to operate the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps a driver secure during a crash.
questions.explanation: A safety belt keeps the driver in position behind the steering wheel during a crash. This protects the driver from injury and helps them keep control of the vehicle.

questions.question: After starting the engine, the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) light stays on if:

options.text: The ABS is not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: The ABS light should turn on when you start the engine, then turn off. If the light stays on, the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: If there is a cargo fire in a box trailer:

options.text: Do not open the trailer doors.
Cover the trailer with a large, heavy blanket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not open the trailer doors.
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors during a cargo fire. Opening the doors gives the fire more oxygen and makes it worse, especially with hazardous materials.

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to change lanes:

options.text: Do not worry about other drivers.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes quickly, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes during the driving test, check traffic, use your turn signal, and smoothly change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: When it is hard to see other vehicles, such as at dawn or dusk, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your lights on.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights on low beam at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather to increase your visibility.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
The weight of the tire itself

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a specific pressure.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you block other drivers, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers. This warns drivers behind you (where local laws allow).

questions.question: When you start the engine, what should happen?

options.text: Warning lights turn on, then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle starts, warning lights and alarms should turn off after a few seconds. If they stay on, something may be wrong with your vehicle.

questions.question: When checking your tires, which is a problem?

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires that are different sizes.
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Valve stems should not be cut or cracked. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: How can you tell if another driver is distracted?

options.text: They drive at the same speed.
They are focused on their cell phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are focused on their cell phone.
questions.explanation: A distracted driver may drift between lanes, drive at changing speeds, use their cell phone, look at maps or food, or talk to passengers.

questions.question: The air compressor connects to the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Engine.
questions.explanation: The air compressor is connected to the engine using gears or a belt. It can be cooled by air or by the engine cooling system.

questions.question: If workers are in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit.
Drive slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower than the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, follow posted speed limits. If workers are present, drive even slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into storage tanks.
It moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into storage tanks. A governor controls the air compressor.

questions.question: Why are roads extra slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Rain mixes with oil on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil on the road that has not washed away yet. This creates a slippery and dangerous surface.

questions.question: If the ABS light comes on while driving, it means:

options.text: ABS cannot work due to weather.
ABS is being used right now.

questions.correctAnswerText: ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: The ABS light means something in the anti-lock braking system is not working correctly.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection test, which is NOT required?

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is.
Check that power steering fluid is adequate.
Make sure power steering fluid is above the full mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure power steering fluid is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located. Check that the fluid is in the safe range. It should not be above the full mark.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you block other drivers, what should you do?

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers. This warns drivers behind you (if local laws allow).

questions.question: When you are parked on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use only one set of turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Always turn on your four-way emergency flashers when parked on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, what will you be asked to do?

options.text: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
Guess how heavy a load is on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your vehicle completely. You must explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: Before you try to put out an engine fire, what should you do first?

options.text: Press the accelerator to use up the fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: If your engine catches fire, turn it off right away. Do not open the hood when putting out the fire.

questions.question: When should you do an after-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: After every trip.
questions.explanation: Always inspect your vehicle at the end of each trip, day, or shift. Fill out a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: When you do a pre-drive inspection, what should you do?

options.text: The inspection report is not important.
Only read the old report if you have passengers.
Read the previous inspection report, if there is one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the previous inspection report, if there is one.
questions.explanation: The first step is to read the last inspection report. Only sign a new report if all noted problems have been fixed.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, how do you use the parking brake?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull a yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake has a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull it out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: When you start your vehicle, what should the coolant temperature do?

options.text: Jump quickly from low to high.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly increase.
questions.explanation: Watch the gauges before you drive. After starting the engine, the coolant temperature should slowly rise to normal operating temperature.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: To make a normal stop in a vehicle with air brakes, simply press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: Except for straight line backing, how many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position during a test?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two times.
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during most test exercises. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you can only look once. For other exercises, you can look up to two times.
